security.admin_ajax_gate: check_ajax_referer('bpfn-admin-nonce','nonce') + current_user_can('manage_options') on all 3 class-admin.php handlers; check_ajax_referer('bpfn-dismiss-notice','nonce') + cap on class-bpfn-admin.php:330.
security.public_ajax_gate: check_ajax_referer('bpfn-favorite-nonce','nonce') only (read-only favorite display, registered priv + nopriv).
security.notes: wppqa nonce-no-cap flags on the favorite-display AJAX handlers are FALSE POSITIVES — both endpoints are read-only and registered with wp_ajax_nopriv_, so no capability is appropriate. In practice the nopriv registrations are unreachable anyway (display_favorite_count() returns early for logged-out users, class-favorite-display.php:315), meaning anonymous callers never receive the nonce these handlers require.

preference_enforcement_broken.title: Per-user notification preferences are non-functional — bpfn_is_notification_enabled() returns true unconditionally in practice.
preference_enforcement_broken.detail: includes/functions/core-functions.php:154-157 short-circuits: `if ( defined( 'DOING_AJAX' ) || defined( 'WP_SETUP_CONFIG' ) ) { return true; }`. BuddyPress favoriting always posts through admin-ajax.php (DOING_AJAX is defined), so every real favorite action hits this early return before the prefs table is ever read. All three channels (web / email / realtime) therefore report enabled regardless of what the member saved.
preference_enforcement_broken.impact: A member who turns favorite notifications OFF still receives BP notifications, emails, and realtime pings. The prefs table + member settings screen are write-only.
preference_enforcement_broken.action: Needs a Basecamp card. Do NOT fix inside a manifest refresh.

preference_enforcement_broken.title: Compat safety-net re-adds the notification at prio 15 with no preference check.
preference_enforcement_broken.detail: includes/compat/buddypress-compat.php:131 registers `add_action( 'bp_activity_add_user_favorite', 'bpfn_compat_add_notification', 15, 2 )`. The handler (:141-189) checks only for an existing duplicate notification, then calls bp_notifications_add_notification() directly — it never calls bpfn_is_notification_enabled() or reads the prefs table.
preference_enforcement_broken.impact: Even if BPFN-PREF-01 were fixed, this second writer would still bypass the member's choice. Both must be fixed together.
preference_enforcement_broken.action: Needs a Basecamp card, paired with BPFN-PREF-01.

dead_ui.title: BP notification-settings row writes to a user_meta key the plugin never reads.
dead_ui.detail: BPFN_Module_Settings::notification_settings() (hooked at includes/modules/class-settings.php:44 on bp_notification_settings) renders yes/no radios named `notifications[favorite_activity]` (class-settings.php:194 and :200). BuddyPress core's own settings-save handler persists that field to user meta key `favorite_activity`. Grep confirms the plugin NEVER reads `favorite_activity` from user meta anywhere — its own reads go to the {prefix}bp_favorite_notification_prefs table via bpfn_get_user_settings().
evidence: includes/functions/core-functions.php (bpfn_get_user_settings reads the prefs table only)
dead_ui.impact: The row on Settings > Email appears to work (it saves, and re-renders checked state from the prefs table) but the value BP writes is orphaned. Combined with BPFN-PREF-01/02 this surface is entirely decorative.
dead_ui.action: Needs a Basecamp card. Decide: read the meta key, or drop the row.

debug_output_in_production.detail: These fire on production installs regardless of WP_DEBUG — they carry only a phpcs:ignore, not a debug guard. core-functions.php:182 in particular runs on EVERY notification-enabled check.
evidence: includes/functions/core-functions.php:164 ('BPFN: No settings found for user ...')
includes/functions/core-functions.php:182 ('BPFN: Notification enabled check - ...' — fires on every check)
includes/modules/class-notifications.php:104 ('BPFN: Component not initialized, cannot add notification')
debug_output_in_production.impact: Unbounded debug.log growth on busy communities; leaks user IDs into the log.
debug_output_in_production.action: Needs a Basecamp card: wrap in `if ( defined('WP_DEBUG') && WP_DEBUG )` or route through bpfn_log_event().
debug_output_in_production.not_flagged: buddypress-compat.php:204,207 ARE correctly guarded by WP_DEBUG (:200). The ~20 error_log() calls in integration-functions.php sit inside the diagnostic/test helpers (bpfn_create_test_activity, bpfn_send_test_email, etc.), which are unreachable from the shipped admin UI — lower priority, but they are unguarded too.

orphan_keys.detail: Retired with the Enhanced Notifications toggle on 2.0.x. Only surviving reader is the diagnostics dump; defaults to array() so it is harmless, but it is a read-never-written key and root CLAUDE.md wrongly claims it is 'no longer registered or read'.

orphan_keys.written_at: BuddyPress core, from the radios at includes/modules/class-settings.php:194,200

unreachable_registrations.detail: Registered for logged-out callers, but BPFN_Module_Favorite_Display::display_favorite_count() returns early at class-favorite-display.php:315 when ! is_user_logged_in(), so the favorite-display markup (and the bpfn-favorite-nonce it carries) is never emitted anonymously. The nopriv path is therefore unreachable in practice. Not a security issue (read-only, nonce-gated); it just means the manifest's old 'public (priv + nopriv)' capability label overstated the real surface.

three_entry_points.rule: Every custom data store needs frontend UX + backend admin UI + API (global CLAUDE.md).
three_entry_points.{prefix}bp_activity_favorites: PASS — frontend (who-liked display on activity), backend (Overview stats + trending, Tools migration), API (bpfn_* helpers + AJAX). No REST by design.
three_entry_points.{prefix}bp_favorite_notification_prefs: FAIL — frontend (BP member Settings subnav) and a write path exist, but the values are never enforced (BPFN-PREF-01/02) and there is no backend/admin view of them at all. The store is effectively write-only.
